_README: Coefficients for every MODELED (kind='estimated') number in metrics/metrics.db.
Nothing in this file is a measurement.  Energy has no direct source on this
host (no wall-plug meter, no RAPL in the cloud runners) and neither does a
gate-level Fmax (no liberty timing).  Those figures are therefore MODELED:
measured_input * coefficient_from_this_file, and every row the collector
writes from them is tagged kind='estimated' with source='coefficients.json:<key>'.
Change a number here and the dashboard's estimates move; the measured rows
(tokens, seconds, cell counts, coverage %) do not.  That separation is the
point: see docs/NOTES.md -> 'Metrics DB' and the dashboard legend.
Every coefficient carries its own provenance/verified_on.  If a figure is
stale, update it here — do NOT hard-code an estimate in collect.py.

_note: Modeled datacentre energy per 1000 tokens, by model CLASS, including a PUE
and idle/overhead allowance.  Public per-token figures for frontier hosted
models are not published by any vendor; these are ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE
community/academic estimates, normalized to a per-1k-token basis.  Treat
them as a consistent yardstick for trending across runs, NOT as an
absolute footprint.
Output tokens dominate: they are generated autoregressively (one forward
pass each), whereas input/cache-read tokens are processed in a single
batched prefill pass.  Hence the ~10x split below, and the near-zero
cache-read coefficient (a cache read skips the prefill compute entirely).
Provenance: derived from published per-query estimates for large hosted
chat models -- Google, 'Measuring the environmental impact of AI inference'
(2025), median ~0.24 Wh per Gemini text prompt; Epoch AI (2025), ~0.3 Wh
per typical GPT-4o-class query; Luccioni et al., 'Power Hungry Processing'
(FAccT 2024) for the task-class spread -- divided by the ~500-1000 token
response length those figures assume, then scaled by class size.
Cross-check any absolute claim against those sources before quoting it.
inference_energy_wh_per_1k_tokens.pue_note: Datacentre power-usage effectiveness already folded into the class numbers above; recorded here for documentation only (do not multiply twice).

_note: CPU-side energy for the simulation/synthesis work, modeled as
core_seconds * watts_per_core * pue.  watts_per_core is an amortized
figure for a shared cloud vCPU (a ~200 W, 32-core server part at high
utilization, plus platform overhead), not a measured TDP.
core_seconds itself IS measured (/usr/bin/time -v user+sys).
Estimated $/core-hour for the CI compute, used to turn measured
core-seconds into an estimated run cost.  GitHub-hosted Linux 2-core
runners bill $0.008/min for private repos ($0.48/h for the 2-core
machine = $0.24 per core-hour); public repos are free, so the figure is
an OPPORTUNITY cost there.  Self-hosted / Railway differs -- override
with the runner-specific key.
FALLBACK price table, matched by model-id prefix (longest match wins).
The collector PREFERS the per-model costUSD that Claude Code itself
reports in the run result JSON (docker/last-run-metrics.json) -- that is
the same client-side estimate docker/render-metrics.py prints.  This
table is only used when a model has token counts but no reported cost.
Cache pricing follows Anthropic's published multipliers: a cache READ is
0.1x the input price, a 5-minute cache WRITE is 1.25x.
Provenance: Anthropic's published list prices for the Claude model
families (claude.com/pricing).  VERIFY BEFORE QUOTING -- list prices
change and this file is a committed snapshot, not a live feed.  Non-
Anthropic providers (Kimi/Moonshot) are deliberately absent: their cost
is recorded as not_attributable rather than guessed.
Weights that turn the yosys GENERIC-cell histogram into a 2-input-NAND
gate-equivalent (GE) count -- the customary technology-independent 'gate
count'.  There is no liberty file here, so these are the textbook
transistor-count ratios (NAND2 = 1 GE = 4 transistors), not a foundry
library's areas.  Matched by cell-type prefix, longest match first;
unknown cell types fall back to `default` and are also reported as
`cells_unweighted` so a mismatch is visible rather than silent.
$mem/$mem_v2 cells are NOT given a GE weight: a 512 Kbit memory array is
a macro, not random logic, and folding it into a GE number would swamp
the bridge logic the metric exists to track.  Memory is reported
separately as `memory_bits`.
Crude Fmax estimate from the yosys generic-cell netlist: the longest
topological combinational path (yosys `ltp`, measured in CELL LEVELS) is
multiplied by an assumed per-level delay, plus a fixed setup/clk-q
overhead.  There is NO liberty file and NO placement -- this is a
technology-independent sanity number whose only real use is TRENDING
(did a change deepen the critical path?).  Never quote it as a timing
result.
ns_per_level is a generic-cell rule of thumb for a mature (~28 nm-class)
standard-cell process at nominal conditions; overhead_ns covers
register clk->q + setup + a clock-uncertainty allowance.
Trend/regression policy used by metrics/dashboard.py.  `direction` says
which way is GOOD for a metric name (matched by exact name, then by
suffix); `tolerance_pct` is the dead-band below which a change is noise
rather than a flagged regression.
